Subject: Mid-cycle usage spike — uplift options and co-terming

Hi Dylan,

Quick note from Novus — we had a higher-than-expected model runway this quarter and we’re looking to increase committed capacity mid-contract. Procurement looped me in to understand our options. Two asks: 1) can you outline a way to add units now without pushing us into a new 12-month invoice cycle (we prefer to keep our June co-term), and 2) what discount/credit options exist for a phased top-up vs. a single bulk uplift?

We’re sensitive to invoice timing and want predictable unit economics for the rest of the year. If you can share a simple comparison (prorate + invoice split vs. annualize for remainder + credit), that’d be hugely helpful.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if easier.

— Claire

Hi Claire — thanks for the note and the usage snapshot. Short answer: yes, we can add capacity without forcing an annual reset. I’ve sketched two practical paths below and attached a spreadsheet (Novus_Uplift_Schedule_v2.xlsx) with the math.

Option A — Phased top-up (preserve June co-term):
- Add X reserved units now on a 3-month pro-rata invoice for the remainder of the current billing period.
- Start a small recurring top-up for the next 3 months to smooth monthly cashflow.
- On your June co-term we consolidate the added units into the annual commit and apply a usage credit for the pro-rated months.
- Typical discount: small incremental discount on the new units (3–6%) depending on volume.

Pros: preserves co-term, predictable monthly charges, minimal legal churn.
Cons: slightly higher unit rate during pro-rated months.

Option B — Annualize remainder immediately (move to new commit slice):
- Annualize the uplift at a blended rate for the remaining term (effectively convert the uplift into remaining-months of annual pricing).
- One consolidated invoice and a modest one-time credit that reflects remaining months.
- Typical discount: 8–12% (volume & term dependent).

Pros: best unit economics, simpler accounting after the single invoice.
Cons: requires a short amendment and invoice alignment to the new commit slice.

Operational notes: we can also do a hybrid — phased billing for the first N months + automatic consolidation at co-term with a pre-agreed credit (this is what the attached schedule models). If you want, I can add an executive credit line (one-time) to bridge timing mismatch; I’ll loop Kimberly for approval if that’s desired.

Next step: tell me which economic/operational tradeoff you prefer (smooth cashflow vs. best unit price) and I’ll produce a redlineable SOW amendment and an invoice sample. If helpful, I’m available Thu 10–10:30am PT.

Best,
Dylan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Claire / Dylan — quick follow from a pricing perspective. Two practical suggestions that usually help close this sort of uplift cleanly: 

1) Offer a one-time timing credit (we’ve used a $Xk bridge credit in similar accounts) that neutralizes the short-term higher pro-rate rate, in exchange for locking the consolidated add-on at a 2% deeper discount at co-term.

2) If Novus is comfortable with a modest auto-topup cap (e.g., allow up to 20% monthly burst without re-approval), we can offer stepped discounts on the incremental bucket (0–10% extra = 4% discount, 10–20% = 7% discount). That reduces procurement friction.

Operational checklist for either path: 
- Legal: single-line SOW amendment referencing existing SOW (no new term length).
- Billing: split invoice option if Option A chosen (we can produce 1–2 invoices to stage cashflow).
- CS/Onboarding: same-day capacity provisioning after PO/ack.

If you want executive credit I’ll need a brief blast email to my manager (cc Marissa) with why — I can push a one-off. Happy to do call to finalize wording.

— Kimberly
Sr. Sales Operations Manager — Redwood Inference
